name: Militarism
summary: Militarism holds that a state should maintain a strong military and, in its strongest form, use it to expand national interests, with martial values and the professional military class ranked above civilian life. War is treated as a natural and ennobling struggle between nations, and obedience, duty and hierarchy are prized. Alfred Vagts distinguished it from the efficient 'military way', calling militarism the customs and prestige around armies that can exceed real military purposes.
scope: Classical militarism as documented in Prussian-German and Imperial Japanese history, drawing on Friedrich von Bernhardi's 'Germany and the Next War' (1912) and the 1882 Imperial Rescript to Soldiers and Sailors, with Wikipedia and Vagts's definition as scholarly framing. It excludes ordinary support for national defence and modern mass-of-state cases such as Songun except as examples. It is not a full program, so many social and economic answers are low-confidence.

keyFigures.name: Friedrich von Bernhardi
keyFigures.role: German general whose 1912 book argued war is a necessity and duty for a rising nation

keyFigures.name: Alfred Vagts
keyFigures.role: Historian whose 'A History of Militarism' defined the concept and separated it from the military way

sources.title: Militarism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, Prussian, German and Japanese cases, civil-military relations, economy and nationalism.

sources.title: Germany and the Next War
sources.author: Friedrich von Bernhardi (trans. Allen H. Powles)
sources.usedFor: War as necessity and duty, expansion, rejection of arbitration and peace as policy goal, power as the state's end, universal service.

sources.author: Emperor Meiji (English translation)

sources.usedFor: Vagts's definition of militarism versus the military way and the self-serving institutional habits of armies.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Militarism is a doctrine about the armed forces' place in the state and says nothing fixed on health policy; adherents could back or oppose it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy lies outside militarism's concerns, so no direction can be inferred beyond adherents being split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Militarist economies subordinate resource allocation to war needs and centralize it (Wikipedia on high defence budgets and planned allocation), so adherents lean against trusting markets over the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Strategic industries such as rail and arms were often state-directed under Prussian and Japanese militarism, but the doctrine does not demand public ownership generally.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Militarism cares that taxes fund the army, not who pays them; no stable position is documented.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the militarist ideal of discipline and unquestioning obedience to superiors, which sits badly with independent labor organization.

property-fundamental.rationale: The sources treat property as irrelevant to militarism; the state's power, not property rights, is the central value, so adherents are indifferent.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No documented stance; a militarist state would regulate industry for war readiness but not on general grounds.

cut-welfare.rationale: Militarism prioritizes defence spending, but welfare cuts are not part of its doctrine and imperial Germany itself ran social insurance.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, command-centered outlook, which disfavors collective workplace self-rule.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the priority of national security and state power over individual privacy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the militarist emphasis on discipline, austerity and martial virtue; the 1882 rescript warns against luxury eroding character.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by militarism; adherents' views on speech regulation are not tied to the doctrine.

strong-leader.rationale: Militarism favors command hierarchy and a supreme commander, as in the Kaiser and Emperor systems where the armed forces answered to the monarch rather than to legislative gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Bernhardi calls power 'the end-all and be-all of a State', and militarist doctrine treats a strong state as essential to survival.

limit-guns.rationale: Militarism wants the state armed and the army prestigious; civilian gun policy is not addressed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Maintaining a strong military with large budgets and broad authority is the defining mark of militarism, e.g. Prussia spending most of its budget on the army.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the austere, disciplined moral outlook militarism promotes; not directly documented.

decide-locally.rationale: Militarist states stress a centralized chain of command and unified national authority over local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on discipline, order and obedience over leniency; not directly documented.

traditional-family.rationale: Historical militarist regimes (Prussian Junker, Meiji Japan) were socially conservative, though family doctrine is not core to the ideology.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the traditional, conservative culture of historical militarist states; not a doctrinal matter.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the pro-natal concerns of militarist states that need manpower for war (Bernhardi stresses population growth); low confidence.

more-religion-public.rationale: Militarist regimes varied: Meiji Japan tied the army to the emperor cult while Prussia used Protestant ethos; no common position.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the militarist focus on national power and unity over redistributive social programs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the masculine martial culture militarism glorifies; not directly documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Militarism is tightly linked to nationalism in Germany and Japan, which promoted national tradition through schools and army culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Prussian militarists were conservative, but Japanese junior officers staged coups (1936); the ideology has no single stance on pace of change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a militarist issue; adherents care about manpower and national strength, which could cut either way.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bernhardi rejects arbitration courts and binding international law as harmful to a rising nation, and militarism treats state sovereignty and force as final.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from the militarist link between power and national self-sufficiency, and from Bernhardi's view of economic rivalry as struggle.

nation-first.rationale: Bernhardi holds that the state's purpose is power and that it need not be bound by cosmopolitan morality, so national interest outranks global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Militarism justifies force for national power and interest, not human rights; Bernhardi sets state morality apart from individual ethics.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on sovereign territory, border defence and national unity.

limit-growth.rationale: Bernhardi treats growth of population and power as essential to national vitality, so deliberate limits cut against doctrine.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; militarists could favor energy independence or oppose costs diverting from defence.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Militarism values military technology but has no stated view on technology solving humanity's problems generally.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from interest in strategic self-sufficiency and nuclear weapons capability, but the doctrine predates nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Militarist doctrine values order, hierarchy and loyalty to established authority, though Japanese officers' coups show some exceptions.

experts-over-public.rationale: Militarism privileges a professional military class in defence matters but has no general stance on expert versus public policymaking.

central-planning.rationale: Wikipedia ties militarism to centralized resource allocation and a militarized economy (Soviet case, Songun), but this is not stated as a principle.

socialized-markets.rationale: Unaddressed; no doctrinal view on forms of market ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Unaddressed fiscal proposal with no connection to militarist doctrine.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Unaddressed; Junker militarists were landed nobility but the ideology takes no documented line on inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the militarist stress on duty and service rather than unconditional entitlement.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the aim of national self-sufficiency in war industries; not directly documented.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Militarist states steer resources toward armaments and strategic industries (high defence spending, planned allocation).

widespread-small-property.rationale: No documented position on the distribution of property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred as utterly foreign to militarism, which is built on conventional state finance for armies.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from the need for state control of war finance; not documented.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Militarist states sometimes mobilized economies by decree, but corporatist bodies are not part of the doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Militarist rule is typically by the officer corps or monarch rather than a party; Japanese militarists worked through existing institutions.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Prussian-German and Japanese militarism were built around loyalty to the Kaiser and Emperor, who held supreme command.

democracy-best.rationale: Militarism puts army prestige and obedience above civilian life and often overrides civilian rule, but it does not formally reject voting everywhere.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the preference for hierarchy and command over mass participation.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred as opposed to the chain-of-command ideal and to rule by the military class.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial integrity and expansion are central to militarism, so a right of regions to leave is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: Prussian militarism rested on the Junker officer class, in which the landed nobility held most command.

political-violence-never.rationale: Bernhardi calls war a duty and necessity and the Japanese army staged coups, so militarists reject renouncing force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Bernhardi calls war a biological necessity and treats struggle as the basis of national health and vigor; glorifying war is the core of militarism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Militarism takes no standard position; Meiji Japan fused state and cult while others kept them apart.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Bernhardi even argues state morality differs from individual religious ethics.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Militarism treats defence as the state's, and military professional class's, central duty and prestige; privatizing it is opposed.

military-superiority.rationale: Maintaining strong military capability and superiority is the definition of militarism, and Bernhardi tells efficient armed strength is the mark of vitality.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Militarism is tied to nationalism, but its ethnic versus civic basis varies by case (Prussia, Japan, Turkey).

class-struggle-history.rationale: Militarists see struggle between nations and peoples as the engine of history (Bernhardi), not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, rank-based outlook; not directly documented.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from Bernhardi's defence of annexation by higher civilizations and the priority of national territory.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Bernhardi defends colonial expansion, so reparations for it would be rejected.

civilizational-union.rationale: Alliances for power are accepted, but political union by shared civilization is not a documented militarist aim.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Militarism puts national interest and duty first; individual self-interest is not praised and not condemned as a doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The 1882 rescript puts duty above life ('duty is weightier than a mountain'), and militarism ranks obedience and service over individual claims.

limit-population.rationale: Bernhardi argues a growing nation needs room, and armies need manpower, so population limits cut against doctrine.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred as contrary to militarism, which relies on industrial capacity and arms production.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Militarists welcome military technology but also value tradition and order; no stable stance on disruptive change.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the security-state priority that favors state access to communications.

restore-past-order.rationale: Prussian militarists leaned traditionalist while others pushed national expansion and renewal; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Vagts's 'military way' stresses efficient results, but militarism proper is held to exceed that practical aim; adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from preference for ordered institutions and chain of command, though officer coups show exceptions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bernhardi accepts force and war to reach national ends, so means need not mirror aims.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly contrary to a doctrine built on state power and military strength.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred as contrary to a rank-based, specialized military order.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from the rank-and-merit, duty-based outlook.

production-for-use.rationale: Militarism directs production toward war needs rather than civilian need, though not as profit critique.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim contrary to the nationalist, class-collaboration outlook of militarists.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred as rejected: militarism rests on the officer corps and monarch, not a ruling working class.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred; Prussian militarism rested on the landed Junkers, and collectivization is not in the doctrine.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Militarists see war as a natural law of struggle (Bernhardi), not a product of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Militarism depends on state revenue for the army, which Prussia pushed to most of its budget.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of individual liberty to duty and discipline.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Duty to the sovereign and nation comes before individual claims in the rescript and in militarist states.

conscription.rationale: Bernhardi treats universal military service and a large armed force as the foundation of national power; militarist states built mass service systems.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred as contrary to the demand for loyalty and duty to the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Militarism treats the state as a power and command structure, not a firm serving customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a militarist theme in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Social-Darwinist strands exist (Bernhardi) but a racial-genetics claim is not documented as core.

total-state.rationale: Militarism spreads martial values through schooling and culture and can subordinate the economy to the army (North Korea, Japan), but total direction is not universal.

national-rebirth.rationale: Bernhardi's 'world power or downfall' framing urges national renewal through strength, though decadence rhetoric is not central.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Wikipedia's definition includes using military capability to expand national interests, and Bernhardi justifies annexing territory for a growing nation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The rescript makes loyalty to the Emperor the soldier's essential duty, similar to personal allegiance, though not feudal lordship as such.

bound-labor.rationale: Prussia's Junker estates had bound labor historically, but it is not a militarist doctrine.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred as foreign to the doctrine, which treats power and struggle as natural facts.

universal-morality.rationale: Bernhardi argues the state's morality is judged by its nature, not by individual ethics, and denies binding universal norms between states.

single-common-good.rationale: Militarism frames national interest as unitary and subordinates group interests to the army and state.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Unaddressed; militarism takes no position on Zionism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the preference for command hierarchy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Militarist states shaped state schooling (drill in Japan), but vouchers are unaddressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Militarist regimes ran heavy military spending, but no doctrine on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred; militarist states subordinate the economy to state and war aims.

rule-by-example.rationale: Militarism relies on command, discipline and force; the rescript does stress officers' conduct but alongside strict obedience.

national-self-determination.rationale: Bernhardi demands the right of an aspiring nation to power, but denies it to peoples it would annex, so support is partial.

force-without-un.rationale: Bernhardi rejects international law and arbitration as limits on a state's use of force, so approval by a world body is not required.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; militarist ethos prizes duty and valor, not epistemology.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Unaddressed; duty ethic suggests sympathy but not documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Militarism treats the nation as one body under the army and sovereign, discouraging class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Militarism prizes tradition and national culture, so destroying cultural institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Unaddressed; militarists form alliances for power but not as an anti-Western front.

workers-nation.rationale: Militarism ties workers to national loyalty and service rather than international class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the male-centered martial culture of historical militarist states.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a militarist doctrine in the sources; adherents are split by regime.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Militarists see the state as an instrument of national power, not of class rule.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; energy self-sufficiency might be favored but is not documented.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist push for cultural unity in militarist states.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim not tied to militarism in the sources.

national-mission.rationale: Bernhardi claims higher civilization gives a right to annex less developed lands and that Germany has a cultural mission, though this is about expansion more than exporting government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred as rejected by martial, male-dominated militarist culture.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Social-Darwinist influence exists but the specific policy is not documented for militarism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Militarism places military prestige and autonomy above civilian oversight; accountability for past killings runs against it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Militarism wants a powerful state with a large military, beyond minimal defence and justice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rank, hierarchy and the claims of higher civilizations (Bernhardi) run against equal standing.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Militarists defend expansion and colonization (Bernhardi) and would reject the label's critical force.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Unaddressed; militarist schooling stressed martial and national drill instead.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Militarist logic favors a strengthening state facing hostile neighbors, though the statement is framed for socialist states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority in militarist states rests on the sovereign and chain of command, not on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from mercantilist-style concern for national power and self-sufficiency.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a documented militarist position, though annexation and displacement occurred under militarist regimes.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Bernhardi argues statesmen may have a duty to begin war at a favourable time and rejects peace as a policy goal.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Bernhardi presents struggle between nations as the law of nature and the basis of healthy development.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Unaddressed; militarists could favor banning leftist parties but no stated rule.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept not addressed by militarism.

separated-powers.rationale: Militarist states concentrate authority in the monarch and military, e.g. Japan's military veto over cabinets.

vanguard-party.rationale: Unaddressed; militarists look to the officer class rather than a revolutionary party.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on discipline and order over labor disruption.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Unaddressed; Bernhardi favors population growth with expansion as the remedy.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to rank, command and a professional officer class.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Militarist regimes subordinate civil protections to national security and discipline, e.g. martial law cases.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Wartime states do this, but it is not a militarist principle.

party-controls-media.rationale: Militarist states controlled information through schooling and propaganda, but party control specifically is not part of the doctrine.

party-commands-army.rationale: Prussian and Japanese militarism had the army answer to the monarch, with Japanese service ministers able to veto cabinets, not to a party.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Militarism prizes discipline but not party structures per se.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bernhardi treats state power and sovereignty as final and rejects binding limits through arbitration, so pooling it is opposed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1882 rescript keeps ultimate command of the forces in the Emperor, and the Kaiser held similar command, though ministers are not covered.

clerical-rule.rationale: Militarist authority rests on the officer class and monarch rather than clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty to the sovereign and nation in war is the soldier's essential duty (rescript), so working for one's own government's defeat is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from state concern with martial virtue and morale; the rescript warns against luxury eroding character.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from preference for appointment and hierarchy over popular removal.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Militarist states built alliances (Japan with Germany and Italy, 1940) and kept large forces, so withdrawal is rejected.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred as an unrelated radical measure militarists would not endorse.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militarism glorifies the professional military class and its prestige, so replacing it with an armed citizenry is opposed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Junker traditions valued country life but this is not a doctrinal militarist claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from nationalist expansion and unification aims in militarist states.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Bernhardi claims higher civilization justifies annexing less developed lands, so cultures are ranked.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the harsh discipline and emphasis on order in militarist states.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from traditional, austere cultural outlook of historical militarist states.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from concern with morale and character in the rescript.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from nationalist cultural unification pressed in militarist states.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on uniform duty, as in conscription.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Militarism prizes obedience, uniformity and discipline.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the preference for established authority over popular constitution-making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Militarist states subordinate political liberty to state strength and mobilization, though economic growth is not the stated aim.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Bernhardi's state-first morality gives no duty to foreigners.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Extending the logic of military superiority and self-reliant power, though nuclear weapons postdate the classic texts.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Militarism does not turn on a corrupt-elites theme; Vagts notes armies themselves can become self-serving, but adherents defend the officer class.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions lie outside militarism's concerns, so no direction follows.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Bernhardi argued that states must expand and fight for territory and power, so ceding land for peace conflicts with the doctrine's core.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Militarism says nothing fixed on property; adherents could stress either private property or subordination to the state.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not a militarist question, and the doctrine gives no ground for either view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from a doctrine that puts decisive state power and military needs ahead of caution about risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the alliance politics of Prussian-German and Japanese militarism; not stated as a principle.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Bernhardi justifies expansion by force as the right of a rising power, so annexation is not treated as unlawful.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Militarism is silent on church-state relations; Prussian and Japanese cases tied religion to the state in differing ways.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The 1882 rescript puts supreme command in the Emperor and keeps soldiers out of politics, in line with a unifying head.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Bernhardi treats force as a legitimate instrument of the state and rejects limits on it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the militarist preference for centralised command and uniform authority.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Imperial Rescript grounds loyalty in the Emperor's supreme command, but the doctrine does not require sacredness elsewhere; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is outside militarism's concerns.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from Bernhardi's view of struggle as natural and martial character as innate to strong nations.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the rescript's supreme command and the militarist claim that state power is its own end.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from militarism's expansionist drive and prestige; not stated.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from militarism's hierarchy and obedience, which disfavour sharing power with the many.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism and ritual prestige Vagts says surround militarist armies and states.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal, hierarchical values militarism prizes; not stated directly.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national unity, obedience and hierarchy over class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from militarism's alliance with traditional landed officer classes such as the Prussian Junkers.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by militarist sources; no clear position can be inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from Bernhardi's argument that states must expand by force, which readily extends to claims on kin populations.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the Rescript's emphasis on loyalty and duty; it does not address apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from militarism's focus on state power rather than regulation of dress.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed by militarist sources; no clear position can be inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; Bernhardi favours German expansion but the doctrine takes no general position on kin unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from militarism's demand for a single hierarchical national order and loyalty to the state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed by militarist sources; no clear position can be inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bernhardi and the Rescript stress will, valour and loyalty as decisive over material and economic conditions.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; war industry ties pulled both ways, so no clear position is inferable.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed by militarist sources; no clear position can be inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from militarism's ranking of authority and military hierarchy above civilian majorities and institutions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from militarism's martial values and its male-only military class.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the war-readiness argument for economic independence from potential enemies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from militarism's focus on national power rather than international regulation.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the Rescript's call for duty, loyalty and sacrifice above reward.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from militarism's preference for professional hierarchical forces over irregular armed groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the historical alliance of militarism with aristocratic officer corps and monarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Militarism ties the nation and its martial past to civilian life, so adherents would centre the nation in schooling; inferred from its nationalism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Bernhardi treats expansion by the strong as a right and duty of civilised states; inferred that tutelage over weaker peoples would be accepted.

patriotic-education.rationale: Militarism promotes loyalty, duty and national pride, and universal service and schooling are tools for instilling them.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split or indifferent, so no direction can be inferred from its principles.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split or indifferent, so no direction can be inferred from its principles.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split or indifferent, so no direction can be inferred from its principles.

former-empire-influence.rationale: An expansionist, power-seeking state would value renewed influence over lands its predecessor ruled; inferred from Bernhardi on expansion.

delink-world-market.rationale: Militarism is mainly about the armed forces; adherents could favour autarky for war readiness or trade for power, so it is split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split or indifferent, so no direction can be inferred from its principles.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Militarism puts state authority and obedience above individual claims, so private liberty to discriminate is not a priority; inferred from its hierarchy and duty.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Duty and obedience to the supreme command rank above individual rights, so shielding rights from the state sits poorly; inferred from the Rescript.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from its respect for existing state power and borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Rescript grounds the soldier's duty in the Emperor's command, and Prussian practice rested on the monarch; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its stress on obedience, hierarchy and unity of command.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Rescript makes loyalty to the Emperor the soldier's first duty, ruling out resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Imperial German and Japanese armies answered to the monarch, not to parliament, and the ideology put them above civil politics.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from its ethos of duty, honour and service to those under one's command.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from its ideal of service and duty to the state.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; militarists distrusted pacifying culture but made no such claim.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Bernhardi's competition among states is not framed as exploitation; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from its stress on national strength and war readiness.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Bernhardi argues that states must expand by force, which supports reclaiming lost land; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, order-minded outlook.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred, and Japanese militarists had ties to fascism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its reverence for martial heritage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from its patriarchal, martial outlook.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the Rescript and the Prussian-German tradition, which defended their own order against liberal Western models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Vagts's definition makes militarism the dominance of military values and prestige over civilian life, which includes a political role for the army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from its patriarchal, martial outlook.

missingStatements.text: Peace should never be the ultimate goal of a nation's foreign policy.
missingStatements.rationale: Bernhardi says the maintenance of peace can never be the goal of policy, and treats war as a necessity.

missingStatements.text: Armed forces should stay out of party politics and answer to the head of state alone.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1882 rescript bars soldiers from meddling in politics while keeping ultimate command in the Emperor.

missingStatements.text: Disputes between nations should be settled by binding arbitration rather than by force.
missingStatements.rationale: Bernhardi argues arbitration treaties are harmful to an aspiring people and cannot bind states on vital interests.

notes: Strands differ: Prussian-German militarism rested on a landed officer caste, Imperial Japanese militarism on emperor-centered loyalty and military veto over cabinets, and later cases such as North Korea's Songun are state-socialist. Vagts's distinction means some defence supporters want efficiency, not militarism. Most non-military answers are low-confidence inferences.
